background_rationale: An engineer by training, he built his airline career in operations, revenue management and finance roles and was chief operating officer of US Airways and American for nearly a decade before becoming president and CEO.

notable.summary: After American Eagle Flight 5342 collided with an Army helicopter over the Potomac River near Washington, D.C., Isom issued a video statement and traveled to Washington for a press conference.

Reporting 2025 results, American said it had restored its historical share of revenue from indirect sales channels, moved to an exclusive expanded credit card partnership with Citi from January 2026, and cut total debt by $2.1 billion in 2025.
Isom said second-quarter revenue grew more than 16% year over year to a record $16.7 billion, though higher fuel costs held net income to $71 million.

personal_story.hook: Robert Isom earned degrees in both mechanical engineering and English before a three-decade climb through airline operations to CEO.
personal_story.summary: Isom grew up outside Detroit and studied at the University of Notre Dame, earning a BS in mechanical engineering and a BA in English. He started his career at Procter & Gamble, then in his late 20s left to get an MBA at the University of Michigan and moved into the airline industry. At America West in Phoenix, where Doug Parker was CFO, he worked in revenue management, operations and finance; he later ran ground operations at Northwest and served as chief restructuring officer at GMAC. In 2007 he rejoined Parker at US Airways as chief operating officer, stayed in that role through the 2013 merger with American, became president in 2016 and succeeded Parker as CEO in March 2022.
